purpose: Deterministic standards-profile DTMF fixtures for phone-channel-dtmf-receiver: clean tones, named Q.24 Annex A AT&T boundary cases, explicitly defined noise, and a synthetic phone-band channel.
generation: Run python3 generate.py in this directory. The generator uses only the Python standard library and fixed LCG seed 0x6D2B79F5; every output is byte-reproducible.
spec_basis: ITU-T Q.23 (11/1988) supplies the two four-frequency groups, keypad allocation, +/-1.8% sending tolerance, and distortion limit. The selected AT&T example profile in Q.24 Annex A supplies operation at <=1.5% frequency offset, non-operation at >=3.5%, high-minus-low twist from -8 through +4 dB, operation duration >=40 ms, and non-operation duration <=23 ms. Values between 23 and 40 ms are a gray region, not mandatory pass/reject fixtures.

sequence_contract.note: No separate 12-key conformance sequence is supplied. The existing 16-key Q.23 order is the deterministic feature corpus; a future mixed pass/reject evaluation set must first freeze receiver level calibration, thresholds, impairment grid, and rejection labels. A 12-key duplicate would not resolve those missing contracts.

legacy_whole_sequence.definition: 10*log10(mean(x[n]^2 over every file sample)/mean(noise[n]^2 over every file sample)); pauses are included.

active_tone.definition: 10*log10(mean(x[n]^2 over the declared active-tone mask)/mean(noise[n]^2 over the same mask)) = 10 dB before 16-bit PCM quantization. For the unchanneled sequence, the mask is the first 800 samples of each 1600-sample key slot. For the channel sequence, the same 800-sample spans start 50 samples later, matching the FIR's exact group delay. Noise is added across the entire file, but its scale is set only by this mask.

contents.content: All 16 keys in Q.23 keypad order 123A456B789C*0#D, each with 100 ms tone plus 100 ms pause.
Sixteen single-key clips (star/hash spelled out), each with 50 ms silence, 100 ms tone, and 50 ms silence.
Key 5 with both components at the inclusive AT&T operation-frequency boundaries.
Key 5 with both components at the inclusive AT&T non-operation frequency boundary.
Key 5 at the inclusive AT&T high-minus-low twist boundaries.
A 20 ms key-5 burst, safely inside the AT&T <=23 ms mandatory non-operation region.
A 25 ms key-5 burst in the 23-40 ms gray region. It has no mandatory pass/reject label and must be excluded from conformance accuracy.
A 45 ms key-5 burst, above the AT&T 40 ms minimum operation duration.
Full clean sequence plus deterministic noise at 30 or 15 dB whole-sequence SNR, including pauses in the power average.
Full clean sequence plus deterministic noise at exactly 10 dB active-tone SNR under the unchanneled mask.
Full sequence through the course-defined 300-3400 Hz, 101-tap symmetric Hamming-windowed-sinc FIR.
Channel sequence plus deterministic noise at 15 dB whole-sequence SNR, including non-tone samples in the power average.
Channel sequence plus deterministic noise at exactly 10 dB active-tone SNR over 800-sample spans shifted by the FIR's 50-sample group delay.
The exact synthetic FIR impulse response as n,h pairs.

note: The audio is synthesized and level-normalized, not calibrated in dBm and not a real acoustic/channel recording. The fixtures establish deterministic DSP inputs and selected profile boundaries; an unfinished receiver's thresholds or performance are not implied.
